math_tags: measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Ranks documents by how similar their meaning is to a search query, using distance in a high-dimensional space.
why_math: It works because when you position documents so that ones with the same meaning sit close together, searching becomes finding what is nearest, and nearness is fast and cheap to measure.

math_tags: ranking things by a learned score
math_plain: Scores items from different categories by how well they answer a user's question, then ranks them together in one unified list.
why_math: It works because you never need the exact scores, only their correct order, so a rough relevance score that gets the ranking right already puts the most useful results on top.

math_plain: Predicts what event comes next in a story and infers which events cause which, tracing the path of one incident across multiple documents.
why_math: It works because causality has structure: causes come before effects and appear in related documents, so showing how one event reliably triggers others reveals the true causal chain.

math_tags: learning a function from examples
math_plain: Learns to find answers by practicing on chains of reasoning, starting with weak examples then improving through reward signals.
why_math: It works because good answers build on good intermediate steps; practicing on real reasoning paths teaches the system which intermediate steps actually lead to correct answers.

math_plain: Extracts what a person likes from their chat history, stores it, then retrieves it when needed to personalize future responses.
why_math: It works because consistent person traits appear repeatedly in their messages; capturing what shows up often in conversation creates a stable profile that predicts what they will prefer.

why_math: It works because intent leaves traces: words chosen to deceive follow patterns, and images cropped to hide things show consistent cropping marks; these patterns reveal what is intentionally obscured.

math_plain: Searches old news articles for mentions of weather events and assesses how society reacted, combining retrieval and question answering on messy historical text.
why_math: It works because relevant historical stories use similar language and describe related impacts; finding articles using that language finds eyewitness accounts, which directly answer questions about societal response.

math_plain: Records step-by-step reasoning traces as an agent searches documents, building ground truth examples of good problem-solving paths.
why_math: It works because reasoning is reproducible: when a model's intermediate steps match reality, those steps become trustworthy training data showing exactly what kind of reasoning leads to correct answers.

math_tags: learning a function from examples
math_plain: Builds a visual workshop where users design and run experiments simulating how people search, then share and reproduce their setup.
why_math: It works because reproducibility requires capturing every choice; when all setup choices are explicit and versioned, the same experiment always gives the same outcome, enabling trust and reuse.

math_plain: Tests fake users by how realistically they click on results and how accurately their behavior predicts which search system is better.
why_math: It works because realistic behavior and valid system rankings are separate properties; resemblance to real clicks is only useful if it actually identifies which system truly works better.

math_tags: measuring similarity as nearness in a space
math_plain: Scores whether Arabic documents match a search question by comparing semantic meaning, then checks if those scores correctly order search systems.
why_math: It works because language does not change the core idea: if your relevance scores put the best results first, they correctly rank which system performed best, regardless of the language used.

keeping only the few dimensions that matter
math_plain: Represents each query as a small neural network that scores documents, using fewer parameters when speed matters than when accuracy matters.
why_math: It works because the most important scoring patterns are the same at all sizes; discarding the least-important details still preserves the strongest signals, trading almost nothing in accuracy for big speed gains.

math_plain: Analyzes search sessions to find when people switch from looking for a specific expert to exploring a topic, predicting mode changes from clicks.
why_math: It works because interactions reveal intent: clicks indicate successful searches, and successful searches precede mode changes more often, so recent success is a signal that curiosity will shift.

following the slope downhill to improve
math_plain: Plans daily advertising budgets using an AI system that reads campaign content, then adjusts individual bid prices hourly to stay on budget.
why_math: It works because planning and control work together: a high-level plan from understanding campaign content gives long-term direction, while hourly adjustments fine-tune to follow it despite unpredictable customer activity.

following the slope downhill to improve
math_plain: Updates the unique labels assigned to products as user preferences shift over time, keeping them consistent with the old system while reflecting new behavior.
why_math: It works because identifiers only matter if they capture current meaning; aligning new identifiers to old ones preserves a working system while updating what those identifiers actually mean.
